# typesense Provider

Manage Typesense collections, aliases, and API keys. Tested with Terraform 1.15/1.16 and Typesense 29.1/30.2.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "typesense" {
  url = "https://typesense.example.org"
}
```

## Connection and authentication

Set `api_key` or the `TYPESENSE_API_KEY` environment variable. See the schema below for endpoint configuration and environment-variable precedence.

Use the cluster API endpoint from the Typesense Cloud dashboard. For an HA cluster, use its load-balanced endpoint. The provider uses one configured API URL. See the [collection lifecycle guide](guides/collection-lifecycle) for replication and recovery behavior.

For self-hosted Typesense, use your cluster's API endpoint.

The API key needs permissions for the objects managed by the configuration:

| Objects | Actions |
| --- | --- |
| Collections | `collections:create`, `collections:get`, `collections:update`, `collections:delete` |
| Aliases | `aliases:upsert`, `aliases:get`, `aliases:delete` |
| Keys | `keys:create`, `keys:get`, `keys:delete` |

The key data source requires only `keys:get`. Recovery monitoring can use a separate key; its permissions are described in the lifecycle guide.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) Typesense API key with permission for the managed operations. Uses TYPESENSE_API_KEY when omitted.
- `url` (String) Absolute HTTP or HTTPS Typesense endpoint. Resolution order: url, TYPESENSE_URL, then TYPESENSE_HOST with optional TYPESENSE_PROTOCOL and TYPESENSE_PORT. URLs must not contain credentials, query parameters, or fragments.
